Build an adjusted-score reference table bundle

Source: R/api-fair-reference-intervals.R, R/api-tables.R
fair_average_table.Rd

Build an adjusted-score reference table bundle

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fair_average'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  nsim,
  seed,
  contrasts = NULL,
  anchor_source = NULL,
  generating_fit = NULL,
  response_map = NULL,
  anchor_uncertainty = c("estimated", "fixed"),
  gradient_tol = 1e-04,
  method = c("refit", "delta", "bounded"),
  generator_method = c("ordinary", "jeffreys"),
  mc_level = 0.95,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fair_intervals'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fair_intervals'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fair_intervals'
plot(x, draw = TRUE, show_title = FALSE, show_notes = FALSE, ...)

fair_average_table(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  totalscore = TRUE,
  umean = 0,
  uscale = 1,
  udecimals = 2,
  reference = c("both", "mean", "zero"),
  label_style = c("both", "native", "legacy"),
  omit_unobserved = FALSE,
  xtreme = 0,
  fair_se = FALSE,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  xtreme_method = c("display", "facets"),
  reference_plan = NULL
)

Arguments

object

For confint() / summary(), output from fair_average_table() with reference_plan, or a saved mfrm_fair_intervals object.

parm

Person IDs (NULL selects all).

level

Pointwise confidence level in (0, 1) and joint binomial order-statistic Monte Carlo endpoint-enclosure level (0.95 default for method = "refit").

nsim

Replication count (>= 2) and seed for method = "refit" (unresolved refits remain in the planned denominator as +/-Inf, yielding Status = "unresolved_tail" when tail quantiles are unbounded).

seed

Replication count (>= 2) and seed for method = "refit" (unresolved refits remain in the planned denominator as +/-Inf, yielding Status = "unresolved_tail" when tail quantiles are unbounded).

contrasts

Optional named zero-sum Person contrast matrix.

anchor_source

Two-stage anchor-provenance fits, union-event index map (list(calibration = ..., scoring = ...)), anchor treatment ("estimated" vs "fixed"), and stationarity tolerance (1e-4 default).

generating_fit

Two-stage anchor-provenance fits, union-event index map (list(calibration = ..., scoring = ...)), anchor treatment ("estimated" vs "fixed"), and stationarity tolerance (1e-4 default).

response_map

Two-stage anchor-provenance fits, union-event index map (list(calibration = ..., scoring = ...)), anchor treatment ("estimated" vs "fixed"), and stationarity tolerance (1e-4 default).

anchor_uncertainty

Two-stage anchor-provenance fits, union-event index map (list(calibration = ..., scoring = ...)), anchor treatment ("estimated" vs "fixed"), and stationarity tolerance (1e-4 default).

gradient_tol

Two-stage anchor-provenance fits, union-event index map (list(calibration = ..., scoring = ...)), anchor treatment ("estimated" vs "fixed"), and stationarity tolerance (1e-4 default).

method

"refit" (whole calibration-to-anchor-to-scoring parametric bootstrap basic limits), "delta" (analytic two-stage event-covariance propagation), or "bounded" (Hoeffding inequality on declared rating_min:rating_max with category_policy = "preserve").

generator_method

For "refit", "ordinary" or "jeffreys" (\(-\ell(b) - \tfrac12\log|I(b)|\) generator).

mc_level

Pointwise confidence level in (0, 1) and joint binomial order-statistic Monte Carlo endpoint-enclosure level (0.95 default for method = "refit").

...

Unused; must be empty.

x

For print.mfrm_fair_intervals(): A saved mfrm_fair_intervals result.

For plot(): Saved output of confint.mfrm_fair_average().

draw

Logical; print the ggplot figure when TRUE.

show_title

Logical; display title/cautions, off by default.

show_notes

Logical; display title/cautions, off by default.

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm() for this fit. Matching saved diagnostics are reusable; recompute them after refitting.

facets

Optional subset of facets.

totalscore

Include all observations for score totals (TRUE) or apply extreme-row exclusion (FALSE). In ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML, finite direct anchors remain eligible even with all-minimum/all-maximum responses, under both xtreme_method conventions.

umean

Additive origin shift for Measure (not fair-score values).

uscale

Multiplicative scale for Measure and measure SEs (not fair scores).

udecimals

Rounding digits used in formatted output.

reference

Which adjusted-score reference to keep in formatted outputs: "both" (default), "mean", or "zero".

label_style

Column-label style for formatted outputs: "both" (default), "native", or "legacy".

omit_unobserved

If TRUE, remove unobserved levels.

xtreme

Nonnegative correction smaller than the score range for all-minimum/all-maximum rows. Default 0 leaves measures unchanged. Its units depend on xtreme_method; no responses or primary estimates are changed, and this does not correct JML bias.

fair_se

Logical. When TRUE and fit is an MML GPCM fit, add structural delta-method standard errors and confidence limits for Fair(M) / AdjustedAverage and Fair(Z) / StandardizedAdjustedAverage. Person rows remain NA because MML person EAP estimates are not part of the structural Hessian. For RSM, PCM, and JML fits this option leaves fair-average SE columns unavailable.

ci_level

Confidence level used when fair_se = TRUE; default 0.95.

xtreme_method

"display" (default) retains the historical average-score display adjustment. "facets" uses conditional total-score extrapolation for ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML, without group-mean anchors. Supply xtreme = .3 explicitly to use the usual FACETS main correction.

reference_plan

Optional data frame of non-Person facet columns, using the fitted facet names, and an optional positive Weight column. For ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML, adds reference_scores: each Person's expected average on this same plan, using its fitted facet locations and scale profiles. Weights are normalized to sum to one. This distinct target does not replace FairM/FairZ or their administered PCM scale mixture. Primary estimates are used, irrespective of display/extrapolation settings. Scores use internal score units, unaffected by umean or uscale. The result retains the fit for confint.mfrm_fair_average(). For an explicit mfrm_jeffreys_fit, this argument is required and the result contains only common-plan reference_scores, the plan, fit and estimator identity. Other arguments beyond fit and reference_plan are refused: ordinary FairM/FairZ diagnostics do not apply. Inspect summary(result); use plot(confint(result, ...)) for supported interval plots. Direct FairM/FairZ plotting is unavailable for this result.

Value

For plot(): Invisibly a ggplot object. plot_data() retains all result rows, uncertainty labels, monte_carlo enclosures, and notes.

A named list with:

  • by_facet: named list of formatted data.frames

  • stacked: one stacked data.frame across facets

  • raw_by_facet: unformatted component tables

  • settings: resolved options

Details

Two-stage delta and bounded formulas. For stage Jacobians \(H_c, H_s\), anchor map \(A = \partial a/\partial b_c\), cross-derivative \(B\), and target derivatives \(G_s, G_a\), union-event loadings are \(U_s = X_s H_s^{-1}G_s^\top\) and \(U_c = X_c H_c^{-1}A^\top(G_a - G_s H_s^{-1}B)^\top\) with categorical covariance \(V = \sum_e \mathrm{Cov}_{p_{g,e}}(U_s + U_c)\) (Murphy & Topel, 1985; CIEligible = FALSE pending short-exposure qualification). For "bounded", signed event weights \(a_e\) on scores in \([l, u]\) have Hoeffding radius \(r = \sqrt{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha)\sum_e a_e^2(u - l)^2}\) (CIEligible = TRUE, Informative flags bounds narrower than the full rubric range; Hoeffding, 1963).

plot() method: Plot common-plan expected-score intervals

For plot(): Points are common-plan expected scores or declared paired differences. Bars show only available pointwise bounds under the saved method. Missing bars are not zero uncertainty. Plotting never recalculates the fit or removes unresolved rows from the saved result. For refit results the bars show the empirical interval; endpoint Monte Carlo enclosures are retained in the returned table and plot_data(p)$monte_carlo, not drawn as sampling intervals. See confint.mfrm_fair_average() for the estimand, assumptions and finite-sample limitations.

Computes model-adjusted reference averages in score units across by_facet, stacked, and unformatted raw_by_facet (Level key). RSM uses the shared scale; PCM converts each observation's reference predictor using its administered step profile before weight-averaging (Fair(M) / AdjustedAverage sets other facets to their finite means; Fair(Z) / StandardizedAdjustedAverage sets them to zero, which is an expected score at zero reference rather than a z-score).

Extreme-score handling (xtreme > 0): PrimaryMeasure retains the original fitted measure. "display" inverts an endpoint-shifted average for Measure only (Model S.E. is NA; fair averages are unchanged). For ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML without group-mean anchors, "facets" shifts the eligible weighted total inward by xtreme times the smallest positive weight (retaining finite direct anchors unless paired with an unanchored extreme), solves the conditional score equation, and reports conditional reciprocal-sqrt-information SE (MeasureBasis, MeasureSEBasis, ExtremeAdjustment). Fair-score CIs remain unavailable when xtreme > 0.

GPCM and SE caveat: For slope-facet element \(j^\star\), $$\mathrm{FA}_{p, j^\star} = \sum_k k \cdot P_{GPCM}(X = k \mid \theta_p, a_{j^\star}, \boldsymbol{\delta}_{j^\star});$$ non-slope facets use unit geometric-mean slope and average threshold profiles before conversion (a package reporting convention, not FACETS score-side equivalence). Model S.E. / ModelBasedSE and Real S.E. / FitAdjustedSE are measure-level SEs rescaled by abs(uscale) – never use them as \(\pm 1.96\,\mathrm{SE}\) bounds on fair scores. When fair_se = TRUE on MML GPCM fits, structural delta-method Fair(M) S.E. / AdjustedAverageSE columns are added for non-Person facets (Person rows stay NA; FairCIEligible = FALSE, diagnostic use only).

Common-plan Person expected-score intervals (confint.mfrm_fair_average)

Compute experimental fixed-Person parametric "refit" or two-stage "delta" intervals, or conservative finite-sample "bounded" Hoeffding intervals, on fair_average_table(..., reference_plan = ...) outputs from unit-weight additive RSM/PCM JML (ordinary or jml_penalty = "jeffreys").

References

  • Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press.

  • Linacre, J. M. (1994). Many-facet Rasch Measurement (2nd ed.). MESA Press.

  • Linacre, J. M. (2026). A user's guide to FACETS, version 4.5.0. Winsteps.com. (FACETS Table 7 corresponds to the fair-average construction implemented here for RSM / PCM fits; the slope-aware element-conditional construction for GPCM is documented in this help page.)

  • Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43(4), 561-573. doi:10.1007/BF02293814

  • Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174. doi:10.1007/BF02296272

  • Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16(2), 159-176. (Cited for the GPCM slope-aware extension.)

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), unexpected_response_table(), displacement_table()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("confint.mfrm_fair_average", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
d <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
# Calibrate the observed ratings with ordinary joint maximum likelihood.
f <- fit_mfrm(d, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "JML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  optimizer = "BFGS", maxit = 500, reltol = 1e-11)
# The bundled example's rubric is 1--4; declare it independently of sample extrema.
# Every Person is evaluated against these same Rater-Criterion cells.
plan <- unique(d[c("Rater", "Criterion")])
fair <- fair_average_table(f, reference_plan = plan)
head(fair$reference_scores) # Expected average, in internal score units.
# Two replications exercise the API only; they cannot qualify coverage.
# Explicit experimental generator; points and every refit remain ordinary JML.
ci <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), nsim = 2, seed = 71,
  generator_method = "jeffreys",
  contrasts = matrix(c(1, -1), 1,
    dimnames = list("P001 minus P002", c("P001", "P002"))))
summary(ci) # Read Status and Available alongside the limits.
attr(ci, "trials") # Includes unresolved refits and their reasons.
attr(ci, "monte_carlo") # Infinite enclosures expose the two-draw tail uncertainty.
plot(ci, draw = FALSE) # Saved plotting data, including the cautions.
# Deterministic local approximation to the same expected-score target:
delta <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), method = "delta")
delta[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Available", "CIEligible")]
attr(delta, "covariance") # Includes the covariance between Persons.
# Conservative alternative with explicit observed/unobserved plan support:
bounded <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), method = "bounded")
bounded[, c("Target", "Estimate", "DesignEstimate", "CI_Lower", "CI_Upper", "Informative")]
attr(bounded, "support") # Check how much of the plan was actually observed.
} # }
# Continue the confint.mfrm_fair_average() example:
# plot(ci)
# p <- plot(ci, draw = FALSE)
# plot_data(p, "notes")
# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("fair_average_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Use the diagnostics saved with this fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics

# Compare observed person means with model-based scores on a common reference
fair <- fair_average_table(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics, facets = "Person",
                           reference = "mean", label_style = "native")
head(fair$raw_by_facet$Person[, c("Level", "ObservedAverage", "FairM")])
# FairM uses the mean reference for the other facets; it is in score units
# It is a conditional model prediction, not a guarantee of fairness

# Fit the same synthetic ratings by JML to illustrate total-score extrapolation
toy <- load_mfrmr_data(example_fit$dataset)
jml <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML")
extreme_report <- fair_average_table(jml, xtreme = .3, xtreme_method = "facets")
head(extreme_report$raw_by_facet$Person[, c("Level", "PrimaryMeasure",
     "Measure", "MeasureBasis", "ModelSE", "MeasureSEBasis")])
# ModelSE describes the adjusted total when MeasureBasis says extrapolation
} # }
